objective.text: Describe the embryo's size from week 3 to the end of week 8.

body.general: How big is an embryo in its third week? On days 14–15 the disc is about 0.2 mm across [f1]. By days 16–18 it is about 0.4 mm [f2]. The book's 18-day embryo is about 1.25 mm long [f3]. By the end of week 8 it is about 3 cm from the top of the head to the bottom (crown to rump) [f5]. Sources measure in different ways, so these sizes are approximate [f4].
body.mbbs: At stage 6 (days 14–15) the disc is about 0.2 mm; at stage 7 (days 16–18) about 0.4 mm [f1,f2]. The book's 18-day embryo, already stage 8, is about 1.25 mm long [f3]. By the end of week 8 the crown–rump length is about 28–30 mm [f5]. Sizes differ by source because fixed and living embryos, and disc width and greatest length, are not measured the same way [f4].

facts.text: Days 14–15 (stage 6): the disc is about 0.2 mm across.
Days 16–18 (stage 7): the disc is about 0.4 mm.
The book's 18-day embryo, already stage 8, is about 1.25 mm long.
Sizes differ by source and by how embryos are measured, so sizes are shown as approximate.
By the end of week 8 the crown–rump length is about 28–30 mm.

misconceptions.wrong: A week-3 embryo is about a centimetre long.
misconceptions.right: In week 3 it grows from about 0.2 mm to a few millimetres; about 3 cm comes only at the end of week 8.

checks.prompt: About how big is the disc on days 14–15?
checks.why: The book's table gives about 0.2 mm at days 14–15 (stage 6).

checks.prompt: The book's 18-day embryo is about how long?
checks.why: By day 18 the embryo is just over a millimetre; 3 cm is not reached until the end of week 8.
